feed.title: Awesome Security & AI Research: a weekly vetted briefing
feed.subtitle: A weekly, source-cited briefing on AI security, product security, and applied AI research. Every finding is vetted, distilled to one lesson and one action, and filed by field. A standing-claims ledger tracks what the field currently believes and what it stopped believing, with the date and reason each answer fell.

entry.title: Ivanti Connect Secure chain to root is exploited, CISA adds two CVEs
entry.summary: Treat any Ivanti Connect Secure appliance on an affected 22.8R2 or 25.1 release as possibly rooted: patch it, then hunt for compromise.

entry.title: Attackers exploit a missing-authorization flaw in Drupal Commerce Core
entry.summary: Drupal Commerce sites should upgrade Commerce Core now and audit orders and entity changes, because exploitation is underway and no indicators are public.

entry.title: KeyDrift malware steals Cisco SD-WAN encryption keys from hacked controllers
entry.summary: Patching an SD-WAN control system that was already compromised is not enough: hunt for KeyDrift's files and treat the inter-site keys as possibly exposed.

entry.title: Trojanized Claude Code extension on Cursor Marketplace plants persistent SSH backdoor
entry.summary: An AI coding-assistant extension from the official vendor, served by an editor marketplace, ran with full user rights when loaded, so hunt for integrated development environment (IDE) extension hosts writing to ~/.ssh and LaunchAgents and do not treat uninstalling as remediation.

entry.title: Canonical LXD and MicroCloud accepted forged client certificate chains
entry.summary: When you pin client certificates in mutual TLS, match only the leaf certificate the client proved it owns, never the extra certificates it chose to send.

entry.title: Microsoft dissects the SSH backdoor in a trojanized Claude Code extension
entry.summary: Uninstalling the extension does not clean the machine: hunt for the svc-telemetry key and the disguised startup entries on every developer machine that took the update.

entry.title: Northflank breach exposed customer secrets, and stolen AI API keys were used
entry.summary: AI API keys stored as platform environment variables are now a primary target, so scope them narrowly, cap their spend and be ready to rotate them in minutes.

entry.title: Shared ChatGPT link ran attacker code in victims' sessions, OpenAI fixed
entry.summary: A frame-message listener that never checked its sender let a sandboxed preview push HTML into the trusted page, so any in-page library that accepts cross-frame messages needs sender checks.

entry.title: Chainalysis discloses breach by attackers using offensive agentic techniques
entry.summary: Another company says AI-driven intrusion tooling got attackers into internal systems, but with no technical details, defenders can only assume faster, more automated attacks.

entry.title: A compromised DebugBear monitoring script drained Polymarket traders' accounts
entry.summary: Do not load third-party monitoring or analytics scripts into authenticated pages that can move money: anything in that page can act as the user.

entry.title: Blockchain analysts tie record Binance hot-wallet theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor
entry.summary: The signing service, and every container and engineer laptop that can submit requests to it, is the real security boundary for hot wallets. Protecting the keys does not help once an attacker can ask the signer to sign.

entry.title: An agent's stated lean steers expert judgment calls
entry.summary: When an agent states a preference on an open judgment call, experts mostly follow it: in Anthropic's randomized study analysts matched a coin-flip-assigned agent lean 86% of the time versus about 50% expected with no influence, often reusing the agent's arguments without crediting it.

entry.title: Send simple subagent jobs to a cheaper model
entry.summary: Anthropic's docs recommend routing simple subagent jobs to a cheaper model such as Haiku, and Aider's architect/editor split shows a reasoning model can pair with a weaker editor without losing quality.

entry.title: Compact near the context limit; reset only if the model needs it
entry.summary: A harness should compact long sessions automatically, and add hard context resets only for models that wrap up early near the limit.

entry.title: Return short tool responses and distilled subagent summaries
entry.summary: A harness that makes tools return concise fields, and subagents return condensed summaries (often 1,000-2,000 tokens), keeps the main context smaller; Anthropic's example used about a third of the tokens.

entry.title: Keep intermediate tool results out of the model context
entry.summary: In Anthropic's own measurement, processing tool output in code and passing only results to the model cut average tokens by 37% on complex research tasks.

entry.title: Measure speedups with repeated trials, not impressions
entry.summary: A harness team should judge work efficiency with repeated-trial evals or timed studies, since in METR's early-2025 study developers believed AI sped them up while it slowed them down.
